# wallix-bastion_config_wsm (Resource)

Provides a resource for configuring the Bastion's Web Session Manager (WSM) integration.
Requires API v3.12+.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wallix-bastion_config_wsm" "main" {
  hostname = "wsm.example.com"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `hostname` (String)
- `jwe_public` (String, Sensitive)

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `jws_private` (String, Sensitive)
- `jws_public` (String)

## Usage Notes

### Singleton Configuration

There is only one WSM configuration on the Bastion. This resource always manages that single,
global configuration rather than creating a new one — importing or destroying it never removes
the underlying configuration on the Bastion (there is no delete endpoint for it), it only stops
Terraform from managing it.

### Clearing Values

`hostname` and `jwe_public` accept an empty value in Terraform to clear the setting on the
Bastion. Confirmed empirically against a live Bastion: the API rejects an empty string
(`"hostname: A valid format is required."`) but accepts an explicit `null`, which this resource
sends automatically whenever the corresponding argument is left unset.

### Read-Only Key Material

`jws_private` and `jws_public` are a JWS key pair generated and managed entirely by the Bastion —
they cannot be set, only read. `jws_private` always reads back masked (`********`); it is exposed
for parity with the API response, not as retrievable key material.

## Import

The WSM configuration can be imported using any ID (it is always stored as `wsmConfig` in state,
since the API doesn't provide one), e.g.

```shell
terraform import wallix-bastion_config_wsm.main wsmConfig
```
